title: Som Tam (Green Papaya Salad)
subtitle: Shredded green papaya with lime, fish sauce, and peanuts
excerpt: A fiery, tangy Thai salad made from shredded unripe papaya pounded with garlic, lime, fish sauce, and chilli. The contrast between crunchy papaya, juicy tomatoes, and roasted peanuts is what makes this so addictive.
sourceNotes: Som tam originated in the Lao and northeastern Thai region of Isaan, where it has been made for centuries as a way to use unripe papaya. It spread through Thailand during the 20th century and is now one of the country's most widely eaten dishes, with countless regional variations.

content.text: A large pestle and mortar is traditional and gives the best result, as the bruising opens up the papaya strands to absorb the dressing. If you do not have one, use a large bowl and the back of a spoon to bruise the ingredients.
Pound the garlic and chillies in the mortar until broken down into a rough paste. Add the palm sugar and pound again until dissolved.
Add the green beans and bruise them gently so they crack but do not completely break apart. Add the cherry tomatoes and bruise them lightly to release their juice.
Add the shredded papaya, fish sauce, and lime juice. Use the pestle and a large spoon to toss and lightly bruise everything together. Taste and adjust the balance of sour, salty, sweet, and heat.
Transfer to plates and scatter over the toasted peanuts. Serve immediately.

items.fix: Add more lime juice and a little palm sugar to balance it.

items.symptom: Papaya is soft rather than crunchy
items.fix: Use very firm, unripe green papaya. It should have no give when squeezed.

items.cause: Chillies not bruised enough in the mortar
items.fix: Pound chillies more firmly to release the heat.
